changes.before: If copyOf is replaced by unmodifiableList, what prints?
changes.after: Keep a list snapshot that does not gain later additions to its source.

before: List.copyOf makes an unmodifiable snapshot of the elements. Later structural edits to the original list do not change the snapshot. This is a shallow copy: mutable element objects can still be shared.
Expected output or behavior: [A]. Compiler evidence is recorded separately from app reading completion.
Optional local transfer task: Explain what happens if the elements themselves are mutable lists. You may trace it without a JDK; reading completion is not proof of a local run.
after: List.copyOf makes an unmodifiable snapshot: a list whose items cannot be added, removed, or replaced. Later additions to the source list do not appear in it. The copy is shallow, meaning it may still refer to the same item objects rather than copying their insides.

Collections.unmodifiableList instead gives a view of the original list. That view blocks edits through itself but still shows edits made through the original reference. Neither a view nor a shallow snapshot freezes changeable data inside the item objects.
The program prints [A]. The snapshot was made before B was added to original, so it keeps only A.
The quiz replaces List.copyOf(original) with Collections.unmodifiableList(original). That changes the result from a snapshot into a view of the source.

before.question: If copyOf is replaced by unmodifiableList, what prints?
choices: Compilation fails because the original is mutable.
[A] because every unmodifiable list is a snapshot
before.explanation: The unmodifiable wrapper is a view backed by original; it sees the later addition.

after.question: Use Collections.unmodifiableList(original) instead of List.copyOf(original). What prints?
choices: Compilation fails because the original list can change.
[A], because every unmodifiable list is a snapshot.
after.explanation: The view still follows original. Adding B through original is allowed and becomes visible through the view.
